key_insight: Rice husk ash can be converted into silica powder that stays amorphous after 800 °C treatment, but crystallizes into quartz and cristobalite after annealing at 1200 °C.
engineering_relevance: This provides a low-cost, biomass-derived silica feedstock with tunable phase state for thermal spray powder development and coating applications.
method: Chemically treated rice husk ash to extract SiO₂.
Heat treated the silica at 800 °C for 3 h to obtain amorphous powder.
Annealed at 1200 °C to induce crystallization and phase transformation.
evidence_signal: XRD, FTIR, and laser diffraction confirmed amorphous-to-crystalline evolution and a median particle size of about 88.9 μm.
watch_item: Particle size, phase purity, and thermal history must be tightly controlled because over-annealing can change spray behavior and coating performance.
paper_title: Synthesis of Amorphous and Crystalline Silicon Dioxide Powder Composites from Rice Husk Ash for Thermal Spray Deposit
